thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 5xx spike (inference) in az1b - > 3% error rate across inference-prod cluster (rolling over last 3m). Pager: june (oncall)

june (oncall): paging in. seeing 502/504s in the redwood-api-prod -> inference route. can anyone confirm region/az?

lee (sre): I'm on it. dashboards show error-rate concentrated on az1b-local lane, latency also up for nginx frontings. health checks flapping on a subset of nodes.

maya (runtime): stack traces show repeated connection resets to the model backend, kv-cache misses spike. Could be network-level or kernel-level.

sam (platform): I see a burst of ENI detach/attach events in cloudtrail for az1b hosts 10.0.12.* around 1789123380..1789123440. AWS console shows high ENI attach rate throttling on the AZ.

june (oncall): ENI attach throttling -> that matches host-level reconnections, explainable for econnreset. impact on active model sessions?

maya (runtime): yes, model processes are dropping connections and some model loads timeout waiting on IMDS for instance-identity during restart. logs: 
```
2026-04-10T12:03:21Z runtime: warn: IMDS call timeout after 2s (retries=3)
2026-04-10T12:03:22Z runtime: error: model load failed: http read: connection reset
2026-04-10T12:03:23Z kernel: ENI detach event: instance i-0abcde12345
```

lee (sre): also seeing DNS resolver errors from the CNI sidecar — rapid NXDOMAIN/timeout retries. Could be resolver amplification because of repeated DHCP/ENI rotations.

ops-support: customer-facing: a handful of clients report API 502s, mostly high-throughput customers hitting streaming/generation. I tagged support tickets #13245 #13246.

june (oncall): severity? Looks like partial outage for inference in az1b, cross-AZ failover still healthy. propose SEV-2 with oncall lead.

sam (platform): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily reduce traffic to az1b via routing policy to 25% 2) spin up warm nodes in az1c/eu1a 3) apply healthcheck stabilization (increase success threshold) to avoid noisy drains 4) engage AWS to lift ENI attach quota/throttle.

lee (sre): confirming traffic steer now. executing routing change: 
```
# reroute CLI
redwood-cli traffic steer --from az1b --to az1c --percent 75 --priority emergency
```

incident-bot: Traffic steer job created (job_id: ts-1789123469).

maya (runtime): also enabling model-fallback route for heavy customers to smaller quantized variant to reduce new load on nodes: 
```
PATCH /routing/policies/production
{ "fallback_model": "gptq-small-v2", "apply_to": ["/v1/generate","/v1/chat"] }
```

ops-support: posted to affected customers: "We're experiencing elevated errors from a subset of nodes in az1b. We're actively shifting traffic and will update in 30 minutes. No data loss reported."

lee (sre): aws-support-bot, can you open a case for ENI attach rate limit in az1b?

aws-support-bot: Case opened: #CASE-2026-04321. AWS notified of ENI attach throttling; they've requested logs and timestamps. ETA initial response 15-30m.

june (oncall): monitoring: after steer, 5xx dropped from 3.2% -> 0.8% in 2m. latency on az1b still slightly elevated (p95 +120ms) but overall cluster healthy.

maya (runtime): started a rolling restart on the most impacted nodes with adjusted IMDS retry backoff to avoid thundering. command: 
```
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart ds/inference-worker --selector=az=az1b --grace-period=60
```

lee (sre): kernel dmesg on one of the impacted hosts shows repeated `net_dev_watchdog` and `rx ring` drops; vendor kernel patch rolled three days ago — I'm flagging host pool to avoid further automated reboots.

sam (platform): also increased DNS TTLs for our internal resolver upstream to reduce query amplification while AWS investigates. set edns buffers back to default.

ops-support: Logging: created incident status page entry and scheduled a 30m update.

june (oncall): 15m status: traffic steer holding, errors down, AWS case open. changing incident to "mitigated" but keep pager for next hour to watch reverts.

lee (sre): follow-ups: - run a kernel regression for the affected AMI - revisit ENI attach pattern in provisioning code (avoid mass rebinds on scale events) - add a safeguard to runtime IMDS calls to backoff longer when host signals ENI churn

maya (runtime): also enabling extra K/V cache warmup on standby nodes to reduce cold-load model loads when traffic shifts.

ops-support: customer comms updated: "Traffic has been routed away from the affected AZ and errors have significantly reduced. We will monitor and provide a resolution summary after AWS completes case."

aws-support-bot: AWS initial reply received: "We see elevated ENI attach throttling due to rapid attach/detach events from customer-managed automation. We're working with internal team to provide mitigation; suggested immediate step: reduce attach rate and request quota bump."

june (oncall): setting action items and owners: lee -> kernel/AMI regression start, sam -> infra provisioning change, maya -> runtime IMDS backoff + KV warmup, ops-support -> postmortem and customer summary.

june (oncall): handing off to lee for follow-through. leaving oncall at 1789123625. thanks all :white_check_mark:
